title: Prove send, snapshot and chat reach back-tab and minimized terminals
body:
Prove, and fix where wrong, that every control-plane verb aimed at a terminal works when that terminal is not on screen. Since card czysfd that is the normal case: every dispatched worker after the first is a back tab.

Hidden states to cover:
1. A back tab in a stack.
2. A minimized window.
3. A terminal inside a minimized Project.
4. A terminal inside a Project that is itself a back tab on the desk.

Verbs to cover:
- `send`, plain and with --settle-ms.
- `snapshot`, plain and with --attrs, --cursor and --tail.
- Targeted chat delivery: Ready gating and idle-aware delivery.
- `close`.

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE (read in code, only partly proven): terminals are looked up by stable id over every tab (`terminal_location` in src/wm.rs). Undrawn tabs are pumped headlessly (`keepalive_inactive`, and the minimized-window loop at the top of the show path). `stacked_back_tab_worker_keeps_claim_snapshot_and_chat` covers snapshot and chat for state 1 only. Nothing covers send, states 2-4, or settle on an undrawn terminal.

ALSO CHECK: a worker stacked as a back tab may never have been drawn. What grid size does it have (snapshot reads that grid), does it match its stack window, and what happens on its first draw (a resize)? Report what you find. Fix it only if the fix is small; otherwise file a follow-up card.

DONE WHEN:
- A table test over {the 4 hidden states} x {send with settle, snapshot, targeted chat delivery, close} passes, driven headlessly like the existing back-tab test (no GUI).
- Any failing cell is fixed, or the card is blocked with the reason.
- The docs/ file that covers the control plane gets a short note saying hidden terminals are reachable (check docs/ for the existing one; no new file).
- Gate: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --target-dir target/agent; cargo test --target-dir target/agent.

Related: card 0e1tml adds `foreman focus`, which brings a hidden terminal forward. This card makes sure you rarely need to.
